title: Set-valued stalk formula for an affine change of middle scheme
statement:
Let $f:X\to B$, $h:B'\to B$, and $v:T\to B'$ be morphisms of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No integrality assumption is made. Put $X'=X\times_BB'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $E'=X'_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B'_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and $E=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Let $c:E'\to E$ be induced by the projections and $h$, with identity on $T$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Choose geometric points $\bar x$ of $X$, $\bar t$ of $T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and a $2$-morphism $a:hv\bar t\Rightarrow f\bar x$ in the direct-image convention. Let $z$ be the resulting point of $E$. Using strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, lem-trf-point-arrows-strict-local-lifts], put $A=X_{(\bar x)}$, $C=B_{(f\bar x)}$, $D=T_{(\bar t)}$; the arrow $a$ induces $D\to C$. Put $H=C\times_BB'$ and $A_H=A\times_CH$. The two maps $D\to C$ and $D\to T\xrightarrow vB'$ give $D\to H$. Form
$$L_z=(A_H)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{H_{\mathrm{Et}}}D_{\mathrm{Et}}.$$
The structural maps give $\lambda_z:L_z\to E'$. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $E'$, restriction from the pointed triple neighbourhoods of $z$ [lem-trf-oriented-affine-neighbourhood-limit] induces a natural bijection
$$z^{-1}c_*F\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \Gamma(L_z,\lambda_z^{-1}F).$$
If $q:\mathbf{Set}\to E'$ is equipped with an isomorphism $cq\simeq z$, there is a point $\widetilde q$ of $L_z$ projecting to the geometric closed points of $A$ and $D$, together with $\lambda_z\widetilde q\simeq q$. Under these identifications the canonical map $(c_*F)_z\to F_q$ induced by the counit is restriction from global sections on $L_z$ to the stalk at $\widetilde q$. All constructions are compatible with morphisms of sheaves and with the adjunction unit.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10 (localization of the triple site), 2.7 (degree-zero localization/limit calculation, printed pp. 179–180); affine change of all three entries and compatibility with the adjunction arrows. The statement here is the set-valued application of that calculation, not its derived coefficient theorem.
